The fix for A, B, C, D, E and G is open as #800. If you can run `cargo test --locked -p semaprax --lib source_verify::` on that branch, I will fix anything it turns up.

body:
This is a useful finding. In case 14, `SPX-T202` for `w` follows from the refused pattern, so I agree that it should not send an author off to fix a second, unrelated problem. The pinned triple is a regression baseline, not a requirement to keep every cascade forever.

The independent coverage check still matters: a malformed arm must not disable a genuine missing-case error. Please retain a control with a refused pattern plus an independently missing valid case; blanket suppression of `SPX-M101` after any bad pattern would lose coverage.

I reviewed #800/#804 and am implementing bounded lexical-scope recovery in #806 rather than rescanning the whole function at each absent-name read. It must preserve read-before-declaration, self-initializer, sibling-scope and independent closure errors, and must not invent a type or binding after refusal. The complete existing receiver and corpus are being retained for comparison.

I will run only the exact affected owners in the consolidated batch, including the relevant oracle parity cases. I have not yet reproduced your whole 60-case result on the current integrated source, so I am not claiming that result or a token gain. #803's conversion hint has also been incorporated locally, with a clarification that the `usize` round trip requires a value no greater than `i64::MAX`.

Update: #800 and #804 are merged into `wavect/v0-10-0` and pushed. The scoped refused-binding recovery in #806 is also completed and closed. Thank you for retaining the independent-error controls; those remain required.

The current consolidated focused run compiled the library harness and executed the selected bodies rather than relying on compile-only evidence. I am keeping the remaining compiler-budget and cache failures open while fixing them; this is not a claim that the full suite or every probe in this issue has passed.
